To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PEG fusion of severed sciatic motor nerves prevents Wallerian-like degeneration and maintains muscle fiber innervations.
PEG-fused axons maintain their axoplasm and membrane continuity, and prevent Wallerian degenerative changes in their distal segments.
polyethylene glycol (PEG)-fusion repairs of severed sciatic nerves restore axonal continuity, maintain muscle fiber innervation and greatly improve behavioral recovery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms underlying functional recovery after nerve injury, with the goal of developing new therapies that will promote regeneration and recovery of function.
the repair and regeneration of peripheral nerves.
the development of novel therapies for peripheral nerve injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PEG-fused nerves are capable of supporting axonal growth and reinnervating target tissues.
PEG-fused nerves are able to restore motor function by reorganizing the motoneuron dendrites and the axonal projections.
PEG-fused nerves have a greater capacity to reorganize than cut nerves, and this may contribute to the superior recovery of function seen in PEG-fused nerve injuries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PEG-fused axons can regenerate through the distal nerve segment, but they do not regenerate at the same rate as the host axons.

the PEG-fusion method of repairing severed axons preserves the axoplasmic continuity, maintains muscle fiber re-innervation, and greatly facilitates the recovery of voluntary behaviors, and these effects are associated with reorganization of spinal motoneuron connectivity.
the polyethylene glycol repair of a single cut or ablation injury to a sciatic nerve preserves spinal motoneuron morphology and connectivity, but reorganizes the latter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
spinal reorganization may play a role in the behavioral recovery that is seen after PEG repair of severed sciatic nerves.

the PEG fusion repair technique is a promising strategy for peripheral nerve regeneration, and that the PEG repair is able to maintain the connectivity and dendritic morphology of spinal motoneurons, which are important for the recovery of voluntary behaviors after peripheral nerve injury.
PEG-fused axons are able to form functional synapses with their targets and that PEG-fusions may be able to restore functional connections between spinal motoneurons and their muscle targets.
